back_cover.headline: Weather triggers. People decide who survives.
paragraphs: Pakistan, 2022: one-third of the country under water, 33 million people affected. Texas, 2021: 4.4 million customers without power, and most of the dead were not killed by the storm. Europe, 2022: 61,672 heat deaths on a continent that had twenty years of heat plans behind it.

This book takes apart one sentence that is often repeated but rarely tested: climate disasters are social disasters. The physical hazard is real, but the death toll is set by things people build — where houses are placed, who is on the vulnerability list, whether a warning arrives as an instruction, and who can afford to leave.
Nineteen chapters, five parts: diagnosis, vulnerability, capacity, decisions, action. Every chapter ends with the observation that would prove it wrong.
bullets: Separates hazard, exposure, and vulnerability — three things usually treated as one
